headline: Interpretable ADMET models extend to cyclic peptides and drug-interaction benchmarks
label: Admet Prediction Models And Benchmarks
summary: Recent preprints and papers test ADMET models on cyclic peptides, drug-food pairs and split-dependent interaction benchmarks.
synthesis: The common thread is machine learning for ADMET and interaction prediction, with evaluation under constrained data and held-out splits receiving increasing attention. AIO applies solvent-aware contrastive pretraining within an interpretable multimodal design to cyclic peptides and macrocycles. hdADMET combines heterogeneous network embeddings with a kernel-based deep neural network for multitask ADMET prediction, while HyperDFI applies hypergraph-graph contrastive learning to drug-food interactions. A JCIM study of surrogate ADME models trained on more than 270,000 compounds with synthetic labels across 25 endpoints reports multitask GNNs with uncertainty estimates, addressing the transition from synthetic labels to experimental data. The drug-drug interaction benchmark shows that molecular representation rankings shift across four chemical-overlap holdout regimes, suggesting that split design should be reported alongside model comparisons. Together these items emphasise evaluation rigour as much as new architectures.
